newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Ashton welcomes Angolan government of unity.
newsitem.headline: Ashton welcomes Angolan government of unity.

text.p: Australian diamond miner Ashton Mining Ltd on Tuesday welcomed the recent formation of a government of unity in war-scarred Angola where the company hopes to tap the country's enormous wealth in diamonds.
Ashton chief executive John Robinson told the firm's annual meeting that the new government was a sign of progress.
"That's a very strong indication of general progress there and for us gaining access to those areas and beginning to develop production," he told shareholders in Melbourne.
The government of unity, formed last Friday, comprises representatives of political groups which fought a civil war for nearly two decades before agreeing to a peace process in 1994.

The former rebel National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA) controls the Cuango River area of north Angola where Ashton and its partner, Sociedade De Desenvolvimento Mineiro de Angola SARL (SDM), have mining title.
UNITA has been mining alluvial diamonds along the river since 1992, Robinson told reporters after the meeting.
UNITA and its old foe, the formerly Marxist Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA), are both part of the new government.
Ashton chairman Nobby Clark told shareholders the Cuango project was potentially as big in revenue terms as Ashton's 40.1 percent owned Argyle mine, the world's biggest diamond mine.
Total Argyle diamond sales for 1996 were US$350.2 million.
Ashton is about 47 percent owned by Malaysia Mining Corp.
